paragraphs.title: Zedekiah’s Reign, the Request for Prayer, and the Chaldeans’ Withdrawal

answers: Zedekiah the son of Josiah
Pharaoh king of Egypt
Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
easy.explanation: Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah.
easy.q: Who reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim?

answers: The Chaldeans
The prophet Jeremiah
The king of Egypt
easy.explanation: Zedekiah sent Jehucal and Zephaniah to Jeremiah, saying, “Pray now unto the Lord our God for us.”
easy.q: To whom did King Zedekiah send messengers to ask for prayer?

answers: The people of the land
The army of Judah
The Chaldeans
easy.explanation: The Chaldeans departed from Jerusalem when they heard tidings of Pharaoh’s army.
easy.q: Who departed from Jerusalem when they heard news of Pharaoh’s army?

answers: He did not hearken unto the Lord’s words, yet he asked Jeremiah to pray
He obeyed the Lord’s words, yet refused to pray
He left Jerusalem, yet asked the Chaldeans for help
medium.explanation: Zedekiah did not hearken unto the Lord’s words, but he still asked Jeremiah to pray for them.
medium.q: What contrast is shown between Zedekiah’s conduct and his request to Jeremiah?

answers: Because Jeremiah left the city
Because Pharaoh’s army had come forth from Egypt
Because Zedekiah surrendered to them
medium.explanation: The Chaldeans heard tidings of Pharaoh’s army and departed from Jerusalem.
medium.q: Why did the Chaldeans withdraw from Jerusalem?

answers: Ask the Chaldeans to depart
Ask the people to go to war
Ask the Lord on their behalf
medium.explanation: Zedekiah asked Jeremiah to pray unto the Lord their God for them.
medium.q: What did Zedekiah mean by asking Jeremiah to pray for them?

answers: He recognized the danger but did not change his response to the Lord’s word
He had already accepted Jeremiah’s prophecy
He had left Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: His request for prayer appears alongside the statement that he and the people did not hearken unto the Lord’s words.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Zedekiah’s request for prayer even though he did not obey the Lord?

answers: Jeremiah was imprisoned, Zedekiah was made king, and the Chaldeans withdrew
Zedekiah reigned, he asked for prayer, and Pharaoh’s army caused the Chaldeans to withdraw
Pharaoh’s army withdrew, Zedekiah reigned, and the people asked for prayer
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes Zedekiah’s reign, then his request for prayer, and then the Chaldeans’ departure.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described in these verses?

answers: They had permanently ended the war
They had surrendered to Judah’s king
Their withdrawal was connected with the arrival of Pharaoh’s army
challenge.explanation: The Chaldeans departed after hearing tidings of Pharaoh’s army, which had come forth from Egypt.
challenge.q: What does the Chaldeans’ departure show about the situation at that time?

paragraphs.title: The Prophecy of the Chaldeans’ Return and the City’s Destruction

answers: Egypt
Jerusalem
Babylon
easy.explanation: Pharaoh’s army would return to Egypt into their own land.
easy.q: Where would Pharaoh’s army return, according to the Lord’s word?

answers: Ask for peace
Fight against Jerusalem and take it
Help Judah
easy.explanation: The Chaldeans would come again, fight against the city, and take it.
easy.q: What would the Chaldeans do when they returned?

answers: It would be rebuilt
It would remain unchanged
It would be burned with fire
easy.explanation: The prophecy says that the Chaldeans would take the city and burn it with fire.
easy.q: What would happen to the city after the Chaldeans took it?

answers: Both armies would bring help to Jerusalem
Pharaoh’s army would return to Egypt, while the Chaldeans would return to fight the city
The Chaldeans would return to Egypt after Pharaoh’s army
medium.explanation: Pharaoh’s army would return to Egypt, but the Chaldeans would come again against Jerusalem.
medium.q: What relationship does the prophecy show between Pharaoh’s return and the Chaldeans’ return?

answers: Because they were going to return and fight the city
Because they had already conquered Egypt
Because Judah’s army would join them
medium.explanation: The Lord warned that the Chaldeans would not depart permanently but would come again.
medium.q: Why should the people not trust that the Chaldeans had gone away permanently?

answers: Do not send messengers
Do not build walls
Do not mislead yourselves
medium.explanation: The people were warned not to believe the false hope that the Chaldeans would surely depart.
medium.q: In the statement “Deceive not yourselves,” what does the word “deceive” mean?

answers: It would guarantee the city’s deliverance
It would not prevent the city from being burned
It would bring Pharaoh’s army to help
challenge.explanation: Even if the whole Chaldean army were smitten, the wounded men left among them would rise and burn the city.
challenge.q: What does the prophecy emphasize about winning a partial victory over the Chaldeans?

answers: To show that even a small remnant could still bring destruction
To show that every Chaldean would be killed
To explain how the Egyptian army was formed
challenge.explanation: The example shows that even wounded survivors could rise and burn the city.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the example of wounded men remaining in their tents?

answers: Pharaoh advances and the Chaldeans surrender
Jerusalem is delivered and the city is burned
Pharaoh’s army returns to Egypt, while the Chaldeans return to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The prophecy contrasts Pharaoh’s retreat with the Chaldeans’ return to attack and burn the city.
challenge.q: Which central contrast appears in the prophecy?

answers: The land of Benjamin
Egypt
Babylon
easy.explanation: Jeremiah went forth from Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin.
easy.q: Where did Jeremiah go when he left Jerusalem?

answers: The king’s house
The gate of Benjamin
The court of the prison
easy.explanation: Jeremiah was taken at the gate of Benjamin by Irijah, the captain of the ward.

answers: They sent him to Egypt
They asked him to pray
They smote him and put him in prison
easy.explanation: The princes were angry with Jeremiah, smote him, and put him in prison.
easy.q: What did the princes do to Jeremiah?

answers: He thought Jeremiah was falling away to the Chaldeans
He thought Jeremiah was serving Pharaoh
He thought Jeremiah had fled from the king’s house
medium.explanation: Irijah accused Jeremiah by saying, “Thou fallest away to the Chaldeans.”

answers: Places of worship
Shops for trade
Small prison chambers
medium.explanation: Jeremiah was placed in the dungeon and in the cabins, places associated with his imprisonment.
medium.q: In this passage, what are “cabins” most likely referring to?

answers: Irijah immediately released him
Irijah brought him to the princes, who smote and imprisoned him
Jeremiah returned to his house
medium.explanation: Irijah did not listen to Jeremiah, but took him and brought him to the princes.
medium.q: What happened after Jeremiah denied the accusation?

answers: He left after the Chaldeans withdrew, when the siege seemed temporarily weakened
He left to join Pharaoh’s army
He left at the command of the princes
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah’s departure is described after the Chaldean army had broken up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh’s army.
challenge.q: What can be inferred about the timing of Jeremiah’s departure from Jerusalem?

answers: Jeremiah wanted to fight, but the officer thought he was praying
Jeremiah wanted to go to the land of Benjamin, but the officer accused him of joining the Chaldeans
Jeremiah wanted to go to Egypt, but the officer thought he was returning to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah was going to the land of Benjamin, but Irijah accused him of falling away to the Chaldeans.
challenge.q: What was the difference between Jeremiah’s purpose and the way he was interpreted?

answers: The gate of Benjamin, the princes, the prison, the dungeon and cabins
The king’s house, Egypt, the gate of Benjamin, the Court of the Guard
The dungeon, the gate of Benjamin, the king’s house, Jonathan’s house
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah was seized at the gate, brought to the princes, and then placed in prison, the dungeon, and the cabins.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Jeremiah’s path into imprisonment?

paragraphs.title: The King’s Inquiry and the Easing of Jeremiah’s Imprisonment

answers: At the gate of Benjamin
Secretly in his house
In the land of Benjamin
easy.explanation: The king asked Jeremiah secretly in his house.

answers: There is not
Perhaps
There is
easy.q: What did Jeremiah answer when the king asked whether there was any word from the Lord?

answers: The court of the prison
The house of Jonathan the scribe
The king’s house
easy.explanation: Zedekiah commanded that Jeremiah be committed into the court of the prison.
easy.q: Where did the king order Jeremiah to remain?

answers: Pharaoh’s army would win
Zedekiah would be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon
The Chaldeans would not return
medium.explanation: Jeremiah told Zedekiah, “Thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.”
medium.q: What message from the Lord did Jeremiah give the king?

answers: He did not want to meet the king
He wanted to go to Egypt
He feared that he would die there
medium.explanation: Jeremiah pleaded that he not be returned there, saying, “lest I die there.”
medium.q: Why did Jeremiah ask not to be returned to Jonathan’s house?

answers: He released him completely
He placed him in the court of the prison and gave him bread daily
He sent him to the land of Benjamin
medium.explanation: The king kept Jeremiah in the court of the prison and ordered that he receive a piece of bread each day.
medium.q: How did Zedekiah ease Jeremiah’s imprisonment?

answers: The conversation took place publicly before the people
The king wanted to inquire about the Lord’s word privately
The king did not believe there was a prophet in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that the king asked Jeremiah secretly in his house.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the king questioned Jeremiah secretly?

answers: He contrasted his true prophecy with the prophets who said the king of Babylon would not come
He asked the king to send those prophets to Egypt
He claimed that all the prophets had fought against the Chaldeans
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah asked, “Where are now your prophets” who had prophesied that the king of Babylon would not come.
challenge.q: How did Jeremiah reinforce his message when he mentioned the other prophets?

answers: The king provided for Jeremiah’s needs as long as bread remained in the city
The city had already defeated the Chaldeans
Jeremiah had been released from prison
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah ordered bread for Jeremiah each day until all the bread in the city was spent.
challenge.q: What does the daily supply of bread until the city’s bread was spent show?
